newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were steady to lower on Tuesday with several dealers noting lackluster activity in the spot market.
"People seemed to be concentrating on harvesting (corn and beans) and are not worried at all about feed business yet," a Kansas dealer said.
Kansas City spot prices dropped $3.00 to bid at $98.00 a ton and offered at $100.00. Spot Kansas/Oklahoma interior values fell $2.00 to offer at $113 a ton.
"Today (Tuesday) is not enough to make a market," a Minneapolis broker said.
But "I'm hoping for a little more interest this afternoon and tomorrow (Wednesday)", he said, adding that he believed demand was holding steady.
A Carolinas dealer said the spot market was firm.

"Everybody is saying they do not want to sell anything unless they take care of their former commitments. That makes the nearby real tight," he said. "I don't think the mills (in the Carolinas) are running full bore.

Mills in the Northeast were on shorter time schedules. "It was lesser run times than what we have seen three weeks ago," a Buffalo dealer said. He noted that mills were running about five to five and one-half days instead of six days.
"It is a reflection of a little less run time that continues to keep the nearby market pretty tight," he said.
